neighbours.label: a cell or organism splitting into two (cell division, daughter cell, dividing, duplicating chromosomes)
fire: Errors in chromosome separation during cell division can lead to serious disease.
Each daughter cell must receive a full copy of the genome before the cycle restarts.
Most bacteria reproduce by dividing into two identical cells every twenty minutes.
Before mitosis begins, the chromosomes duplicate and condense into visible threads.
The yeast cell buds and splits into two, leaving a small scar on the mother.
Stem cells in the gut keep dividing throughout the life of the animal.
Once the embryo splits into two halves, identical twins can develop.
Under the microscope we watched the amoeba divide into two daughter cells.
quiet: Errors in protein folding during cell stress can lead to serious disease.
Each mature cell must receive enough oxygen before the tissue can repair.
Most bacteria survive by forming tough spores when nutrients run out.
Before the experiment begins, the samples are stained and mounted on slides.
The yeast cell ferments the sugar, leaving a small amount of alcohol behind.
Stem cells in the gut keep secreting mucus throughout the life of the animal.
Once the embryo implants in the wall of the uterus, the placenta can develop.
Under the microscope we watched the amoeba engulf a small piece of food.
